profile.headline: Full-Stack Software Engineer @ BioIntelliSense | Python • AWS • .NET
profile.summary:
Science at the heart of everything I do.

I'm a Full-Stack Software Engineer with a background in NanoEngineering and Chemistry. I've run reactions, used scientific tooling firsthand, and been the end user I now build for. That shapes how I approach software: with domain context and an instinct for what matters most to the people using the tools.

I build things that didn't exist before, because they needed to. I'm most effective on unstructured problems, working directly with end users to understand their pain points, navigate ambiguity, and make sure we're solving the right thing. By distilling a tool to its core function (despite what the label says it's for), I'm resourceful in adapting existing systems in ways that aren't obvious from the outside.

Core Competencies
Full-Stack: .NET/Blazor, Node.js, SQL
Data & IoT: Databricks, IoT monitoring (5K+ devices), Python ETL
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS/EC2), Terraform, Auth0/RBAC
AI Tooling: Claude Code, LLM Integration, Prompt Engineering

positions.title: Software Engineer, Solution Engineering
positions.description:
Led development of an internal operations platform serving 200+ users across device lifecycle management and patient processing. Built full-stack solutions using .NET/Blazor, MongoDB Atlas, and AWS infrastructure with focus on HIPAA-adjacent security controls and operational efficiency.

Key contributions:
- Architected enterprise security infrastructure implementing Auth0 RBAC, JWT authorization, AWS VPC peering, and TLS encryption
- Implemented Databricks dashboards monitoring 5K+ IoT devices, cutting mean time to resolution by 40%
- Designed comprehensive audit log framework to meet security and compliance requirements, implementing MongoDB schema and indexing strategy that enables sub-second retrieval across documents
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Technical Solution Design · Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) · Python (Programming Language) · C# · JavaScript · MongoDB · Databricks · Auth0

positions.title: Project Manager
positions.description:
Drove product adoption and user satisfaction across a 1,500+ user base by leading usability studies, analyzing user behavior data, and partnering with engineering teams to prioritize high-impact features. Bridged technical and business stakeholders to translate user feedback into actionable product improvements.

Key contributions:
- Achieved 90% product adoption through data-driven UI/UX enhancements and feature prioritization
- Reduced average ticket resolution time by 22% by analyzing user-reported issues and creating detailed technical specifications with reproduction steps
- Improved user satisfaction by 30% through systematic analysis of system telemetry and behavior patterns
positions.insights: Skills: Stakeholder Management · Requirements Analysis · Problem Solving

positions.title: Research Associate
positions.description:
Developed automated systems for high-throughput experimentation using nanoscale synthesis, focusing on data pipeline automation and analysis workflows. Built Python-based solutions to process and analyze large-scale screening data for drug discovery programs.

Key contributions:
- Engineered Python ETL pipelines automating integration of 100K+ daily data points from high-throughput screening assays, improving hit identification accuracy by 35%
- Designed scalable data pipelines that automated experimental workflows from collection through analysis and reporting
- Reduced data processing time by 50% and eliminated manual entry errors through end-to-end pipeline automation

volunteerExperiences.description:
I joined the Triton Engineering Student Council as a member of their Executive Board to contribute to UCSD's engineering community. I firmly believe that student led initiatives help empower and inspire creative solutions to common problems. By partnering with different STEM companies, TESC delivers an engaging experience for recruiters, mentors, and students, allowing them to network and learn from each other. In this capacity, I:

• Partnered with 22 companies to support student-led initiatives, resulting in a budget of $200K+ to support hackathons, career development events, and youth outreach programs
• Improved student-recruiter engagement by 62% by introducing mock interviews and “sponsor passports”
• Hosted workshops to train new council members on methods of strategic planning and resource allocation

Video games are more than just recreational free-time activities - they’re the adventures created by one individual and explored by another. They invite strangers from varying backgrounds to become friends, they challenge teams to develop new strategies, and they encourage aspiring engineers and artists to ideate, iterate, and inspire.

Triton Gaming is a non-profit, student led organization that strives to create an epic, diverse, and all-inclusive gaming environment on campus through engaging entertainment experiences. As the Live Events Director, I:

• Conducted participant recruitment efforts resulting in multiple studies and trial runs
• Analyzed social media interactions and prioritized features to improve retention by 22%
• Led a team of 30 students across different disciplines to plan, market, and host events for 2000+ attendees
• Bridged the gap between industry sponsors and students through Q&A panels, featured demos, and tournaments

projects.title: Functionalized Multi-walled Carbon Nanotubes for Trace Detection of Explosives
projects.description:
The objective of this project was to design and fabricate a low-cost sensor for the trace detection of explosives. While current detectors utilize either colorimetry, mass spectroscopy, or gas chromatography, this project evaluated chemoresistance as a method of detecting common nitroaromatic compounds used in explosives, such as RDX or TNT. 

•	Functionalized MWCNTs using 1-pyrenemethylamine and triphenylene
•	Created three different molds for fabrication of the sensor (3D print, 1 wt% agarose, PDMS)
•	Experimented with different fabrication methods to create thin layers: dropcasting, spincoating
•	Collected & analyzed data on differences in resistance between samples
